notes.title: Nalo Tracker app for iOS released
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/8c068c47ddb1cd90e7062bbfd5de68fd99c97f17.png[/img]

Some time ago we launched [url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.myousoftware.nalo_device]Nalo Tracker for Android[/url] devices.
And we're happy to announce that we've finally released [url=https://apps.apple.com/es/app/nalo-tracker/id1602283001]Nalo Tracker for iOS[/url] today.

Running this app on your smartphone will turn it into a foot or body movement tracker and send them to Natural Locomotion for PC where, our locomotion algorithm will convert the movements into joystick/trackpad inputs for walk, run and jump in almost any SteamVR game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/6a7c44362eb4de47ca7b2c48a31ae18eddd184bc.png[/img]

Nalo Tracker app in your smartphone could be used with many different devices combinations:

[h2]Seated[/h2]
[list][*] 1x Smartphone running as foot tracker in the foot.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/38b497441ab2992813c45371e6c02c01ed66147e.png[/img]

[h2]Standing[/h2]
[list][*]1x Smartphone running as feet tracker in one foot and a Nintendo Switch Joycon in the other.
[*]1x Smartphone running as body tracker in the pocket and 2x Nintendo Switch Joycon in the feet.
[*]1x Smartphone running as body tracker in the pocket and 2x Playstation 3 Move controllers in the feet.
[*]2x Smartphones running as feet trackers in the feet. 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/d4f8f64507a0a5ba055fcaeb27fc95a7e535d2a7.png[/img]

Nalo tracker can be also used for make the locomotion direction relative to hip orientation while running it in your smartphone inside your pocket.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/f86be340eebf6cb5e00bd8211e802c5d40279061.png[/img]

Nalo Tracker for iOS also includes some UI improvements over the Android version. We have added some tutorials and tips to the app, as well as a sensors monitor to view the sensors data info.

These improvements are comming soon to the Android version.

Thanks a lot for your support!

notes.title: Vive and Index cameras fixed. Thumb rest touch support Quest 2 + Virtual Desktop
notes.content:
This week we have received the new HTC Vive Pro 2 to ensure full compatibilty with Natural Locomotion.
Natural Locomotion is now reading the IDs of the connected USB devices to determine whether to use a workaround that is needed for the cameras but that could crash other headsets. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/8d5cd50550d6965b79b04e2006d348790a0cf442.png[/img]

We have also added support for thumb rest touch (the capacitive sensor in Oculus Quest 2 controllers) to use as activator to walk. This option only works with Virtual Desktop so far, not with Oculus Link or Air Link (if Oculus adds this functionality it will work automatically).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/0c7c67fb2db68881eefc7166e5b6cf42580a6043.png[/img]

[h2]Changes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Added camera support for Vive, Vive Pro, Vive Pro 2, Vive Cosmos Elite and Valve Index.
[*] Added thumb rest touch support for Oculus Quest 2.
[*] Added thumb rest touch auto detection (if you touch it, it shows a pop-up asking if you want to enable it).
[*] Added option to enable/disable thumb rest touch activator in common settings.
[/list]

[h2]Important[/h2]
If you use a Vive or Index as wireless receiver for Lightouse controllers or trackers (and not as headset) while using other headset you should disable the camera to avoid crashes.

notes.title: 3rd anniversary update: Hip direction for hands mode, Y-pose calibration, & more
notes.content:
We released Natural Locomotion on Sunday, 8th of April of 2018 with just Vive support, a very basic hands mode and a few profiles. Looking back the application has grown a lot thanks to the support of a wonderful community that allowed us to continue the development. For this update we have only a few changes but we hope you like them.

We would like to announce we are working with Decagear team to add support to Decamove as an official Natural Locomotion tracker!
[url=https://twitter.com/MyouSoftware/status/1374050496680452097]We received one a few days ago.[/url]

[h1]New Features[/h1]

[list][*]Hip direction for hands mode: You can now move in the direction of your body in hands mode, with a smartphone in the pocket or with a Vive tracker on the waist.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/9ad41165ce73114fff3f6b67db854035d4f6547a.png[/img]

[*]T-pose to calibrate direction quickly can now be disabled, or switched to Y-pose because the T-pose conflicted with a gesture in Population: One.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/778c07342594b9033319c5f419bc2a46e55cb228.png[/img]

[*]Some profiles now have a screenshot of the settings. Click them to expand. We will continue adding screenshots for all the profiles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/d181c0b71ea200d9b31726b88aca8ef17db48709.gif[/img]
[/list]

[h1]Fixes and improvements[/h1]

[list][*]Fitness stats now makes it more obvious that it's a button that can be switched from "session" to "profile" and "global".

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/7f2eab05c68323cf655916766589c6dff88278a6.gif[/img]

[*]Fixed some WMR headsets jumping all the time.
[*]Fixed foot tracker icons, it was showing generic ones instead.
[*]Miscellaneous UI changes.
[*]Added and modified some profiles.
[/list]

[h1]This is what we have achieved in Natural Locomotion in the last 3 years!

[h2]Hands Mode[/h2]
Slowly swing your hand controllers to walk or move them fast to run. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/cb4456b2d5eac8b9958c0031f1dcdf57ee75b4a6.png[/img]

Other "arm swinger" implementations are very "jumpy", very slow to respond, or are a complement on button actions. Natural Locomotion uses a novel system designed to walk and run continuously, and with very precise and intuitive control of speed and acceleration. You can start, stop or change speed very quickly without "move" or "brake" buttons, it just depends on the speed you move your arms.

[h3]Buttonless activator based on gestures[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/3759b91d6d2580d7792edce376a907f5c19e9ec1.png[/img]

[h3]Hip direction for hands mode[/h3]
As we have announced today, hands mode is now compatible with body trackers (Smartphones and trackers). Using a body tracker, the direction of the movement depends on where your hip is oriented which could make this locomotion method even more immersive and comfortable. 

[h2] Feet Mode [/h2]
Use motion sensor devices (see the list below) attached in your feet to register your feet movements and walk in the game. It supports two kind of movements: Walk-in-place and swinging feet while sitting on a chair or using a treadmill.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/929fe62a5b4a00c4e67a6861c1303bc6c80b7b9a.png[/img]

[*]HTC Vive Cosmos
[*]Pico Neo 2 and Pico Neo 2 EYE
[/list]

[*]Smartphone with Android >= 5.1, with accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer (compass).
[url]https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.myousoftware.nalo_device[/url]
[/list]

[h2] SteamVR Tools [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/70523bff78b8f2aa3550d5643a81e969ded724f5.png[/img]

[h3]Align VR spaces of different tracking systems[/h3]
Combine lighthouse devices (Trackers, HTC Vive controllers or Index controllers) with Oculus, WMR or Vive Cosmos headsets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/c0254d2ad5886a98d07fa47ae5300416674f39b3.gif[/img]

[h3]Convert some SteamVR controllers into trackers[/h3]
This tool will temporarily emulate HTC Vive trackers using other lighthouse devices (And Oculus CV1 controllers) without flashing them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/79428a3a5f182d88273a47921c2286e285bcedf5.png[/img]

[h3]Convert Steam Controller dongles to Vive/Index dongles[/h3]
This utility allows you to convert Steam Controller dongles into Vive/Valve controller/tracker dongles (and restore them).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/9f3d6b2fbc4d8790d74c2fc7438a2118ce24101a.gif[/img]

You need one dongle per device. A Vive or Index headset has two of them built in. For example if you have 4 controllers and an Index/Vive headset (only USB and power connected), you only have 2 receptors and you need 2 dongles to use all controllers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32383436/962735a3a70b5ec801e3eebb7a436afa471bbf26.png[/img]

[h2]Profiles[/h2]
The past 3 years we added profiles for 88 games, which could not be very impressive, but if you count the different profiles for each controller type this number jumps to 476 (not counting Revive profiles).

notes.title: Added support for HP Reverb G2, Joystick tilt, profile for Hellsplit: Arena
notes.content:
We've added support for HP Reverb G2, and created a profile list for it based on Oculus profiles, but using joystick tilt as activator (because its joystick doesn't have a touch sensor).

Joystick tilt has been fixed, and we've added "joystick tilt up" that only activates in that direction so that it can be remapped independently of the other three directions.

HP Reverb G2 profiles by default have this configuration:
[list][*]Dominant hand joystick: Tilting up enables walking. Tilting and releasing up very quickly passes that action to the game.
[*]Movement hand joystick: Tilting on any direction enables walking. Tilting up does it normally (both hand directions are used). Tilting on any other direction it overrides the direction of both hands.
[/list]

notes.title: Half Life: Alyx profile, Seated feet mode and more!
notes.content:
We have added a new [b]seated feet mode[/b] to play with one or two devices on the ankles while sitting on a chair with the feet hanging, sliding, on a static bike or even some treadmills. The direction is calibrated just by doing a [b]T-pose[/b] extending the arms to the sides. It includes features like [b]smooth rotation[/b] (if it doesn't makes you dizzy), and [b]head tilt strafing[/b] (which also works in all other modes). Seated feet mode is not as immersive as standing, however it can be extremely useful in many situations, and it's a good compromise between immersion, convenience and exercise.

This new feature [b]can be used with a single smartphone[/b], which is more convenient than looking for trackers or a second device.

Seated feet mode is also ideal to be used with [url=https://www.indiegogo.com/projects/cyber-stepper-for-vr/coming_soon]Cyber-Stepper[/url]  an amazing device with pedals that track user's foot movements. In fact we have developed this feature with this device in mind and we are working together with Cyber-stepper creators to adjust our locomotion algorithms to use the speed sensors their device, which will make it officially supported by Natural Locomotion.

[h2]New features[/h2]
[list][*] Added seated feet mode which works swinging feet while sitting on a chair and requires a single tracking device attached to the foot (e.g. an Android Smartphone or a Nintendo Switch Joycon).

We added a branch with the current version and the old driver to be used with previous windows versions. To enable it, right click on Natural Locomotion in Steam library go to  Properties > BETAS and enable "old_wmr_driver"
[*] Fixed passthrough cameras of HTC Vive/Vive Pro and Valve Index.

At last, we combined all experimental features in a single version for you all to enjoy!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32383436/660a9d5dcb4cc6b5aeacf0ba387ac9ec607bbbdd.png[/img]

We polished Valve Index controller support, but if you already had Vive wands, you can use them on the feet, or as a tracker in any app. Now you can convert Steam Controller dongles into Vive/Index controller receptors using NaLo, or use them with other headsets, using the new tool to align VR spaces.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32383436/119e2b96df69453fee1924cd323b3acfbb6c169e.png[/img]

We also added explicit Rift S support, with two new activators: filtered joystick touch support and virtual thumb rest (detecting the thumb on the border of the controller even though there is no sensor there).

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32383436/c100ccd0cff2f60c59cb33e6051be03f349371a6.png[/img]

You can use two smartphones as foot trackers, or two joycons and a spmartphone on the pocket.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32383436/b09bd0f1f7a98b5fb3051ea0b5509c704f861466.png[/img][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32383436/d25cb2b28ca7229f7594590ac33a2a6de0ae99cd.png[/img]

[list][*]Added Rift S support, defaulting to joystick touch (with added movement filter).
[*]Add a virtual thumb rest option (for Rift S users used to the old controllers).
[*]Promoted walk in place with trackers (from beta to current), improved UI.
[*]Promoted walk in place with Joycons, PS Move or smartphones (from experimental to current).
[*]Improved foot speed detection (for PS Move/Joycons) and room scale filter.
[*]Fixed smartphone app to work without webview.
[*]Removed all beta branches.
[*]Added support for Valve Index controllers.
[*]Added support for using only the hand controllers as foot trackers for testing.
[*]Improved SteamVR controller conversion into trackers (for use in any game or app).

notes.title: Lag FIXED! Simulation sickness bug in demo FIXED!
notes.content:

notes.title: Added support for Oculus Rift and Windows Mixed Reality! Fixed Skyrim sprinting and zig zagging! Added profiles and more...
notes.content:
This update was really tough. Skyrim direction detection is weird. It's not HMD based or controller based. It's so weird we added its own option:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32383436/13625c7fea729bdc6b9f1582863dc6817575386e.png[/img]
[i]"When thumb moves up, player walks towards Skyrim"[/i]


It was working good enough in Vive by pure chance, because of how the controller is held. But it had a weird spot and was very difficult to sprint. These issues were amplified a lot with Oculus Touch controllers, and we had to fix it before we announced Rift support...

Vive users will also see an improvement with these changes, as the active "forwards" area is bigger. Zig-zagging is fixed and running straight is now possible, which was a prerequisite for sprinting.

Did it improve Skyrim VR for you? Tell us below!

The activation button for most Rift profiles is thumb rest (the little touchpad-like thing).
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32383436/13706529051d5782f92440b4a5dd347291b81318.png[/img]

Full list of changes:
[list]
[*]Added Oculus Rift support.
[*]Added Windows Mixed Reality (WMR) support.
[*]Added headset detection and have separate built-in profiles for each.
[*]Added "Skyrim" direction mode. Removed "Slerp" parameter.
[*]Set not to run game by default.
[*]Added most options to running profile screen.
[*]Added "run game now" button to running profile screen.
[*]Use original left trigger in FO4VR, flashlight is disabled for now.
[*]Removed "palm side down/up" remaps until they're fixed.
[*]Added Vive profiles for Kartong, H3VR, Payday 2 VR, Dead Effect 2 VR.
[*]Added Rift profiles for Onward, Pavlov VR, Payday 2 VR, Dead Effect 2 VR, Stand Out, in addition to the old Vive ones.
[*]Added WMR profiles for H3VR, Payday 2 VR, Dead Effect 2 VR, in addition to most of the Vive ones.
[/list]
Known issues:
[list][*]Some people must enable the "switch controllers" option. And some must have it off.
[*]In Rift and WMR, sometimes it takes a bit longer to stop than it should. To be fixed soon.
[*]Some profiles are not available on all headsets due to current limitations that will be fixed soon.
[*]In Rift in some rare cases, if the demo is enabled, when starting Skyrim a black screen may appear. If that happens, disable the demo in settings.
[*]WMR jump may be too sensitive. It will be adjusted and we'll add an option.
[/list]

As usual, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/798810/discussions]head to the forum[/url] to report issues.
